title: Kankobele (thumb piano)
summary: The kankobele is a hand-held lamellophone of the Ila of Zambia, with about a dozen metal keys laid over a small open calabash. The player holds it in both hands and plucks the keys with the fingers; it also accompanies games.
howToPlay: Every key is lit in order of pitch; the tip of each key is where the thumb plucks.
Notes fall toward a tip; strike it as the note lands. The key flexes and glows.
Start with the first cycle, then the answering one.
rules: A stroke on the pulse is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The open calabash is its voice box: the keys ring above the hollow and the player can open or close it against the body to colour the sound.
credits: Tradition: the kankobele; cycles written for this game
